title: The Teleporting Roguelike
claim: A playable deterministic world can teleport between devices as chain bytes alone, reconstruct byte-identically despite clock skew, accept compatible offline work by declared reads, and reject forged provenance without disturbing the last verified game.
invariants: The map, player, enemies, inventory, combat outcomes, and discovered rooms are reconstructed solely by replaying accepted frames.
Every frame uses recursive lexicographic canonical JSON and browser Web Crypto SHA-256.
Every non-genesis frame names the exact previous verified frame as its parent; device timestamps never determine dependency order.
Device B receives only serialized chain bytes and must reconstruct canonical world bytes identical to Device A.
Device C may reattach offline frames only when every declared read remains a verified ancestor of the destination.
A valid-hash semantic inventory forgery or parent-provenance forgery must be refused without replacing the last verified chain.
positive_path: Play manually or run the guided proof to append deterministic movement, combat, pickup, healing, and discovery frames.
Pause Device A, transfer only its serialized chain to badly skewed-clock Device B, and compare canonical world SHA-256 bytes.
Continue Device C offline from an older frame and reattach its discoveries when all declared reads remain ancestors.
Scrub and replay the append-only ledger while live assertions independently verify the active chain.
failure_path: Append a valid-hash nonexistent inventory use, wrong-parent frame, or unavailable Device C declared read; verification refuses the candidate without changing the accepted head.
